issues.description: Incremental lexical update fails closed while lineage closures retain the original generation; a full rebuild is required. On this repository the successful rebuild takes about 109 seconds, despite only 17 new theorem/audit owners.

The first full rebuild rejected concurrent source changes and preserved the old index. Root had added the final audit while it ran; the quiescent retry succeeded. This was an execution mistake, not a Ladon bug.

maxNodes=3000 returns 666 distinct nodes, one two-edge route and a truncated view, although the closure summary has 2218 nodes. The cap appears to operate on recursive rows rather than unique nodes; clarify labels/accounting before callers interpret this as a unique-node limit.

requested_improvements: Allow new lexical generations while retaining old lineage as explicitly generation-bound evidence, or explain why a full rebuild is necessary in the update result.
Clarify acquisition row versus unique-node budgets and estimate an adequate route budget from the stored summary.
Prior R01: preserve earlier same-file declarations in source-goal completion and fix the single le_trans candidate evidence conflict.
nonclaims: No theorem replay is performed by stored lineage views.
Bounded bottlenecks do not establish mathematical necessity or complete alternative-proof coverage.
This is not qualification of every Ladon feature.
